categories.title: Surveys and Position Papers
categories.description: Related surveys on agent memory, skills, and self-evolving agents, plus position papers.

categories.title: Foundations and Related Directions
categories.description: Mechanisms that experience-driven agents build on (acting, retrieval, cognitive architectures) and neighbouring paradigms such as case-based reasoning, reinforcement learning, and self-improvement.

categories.title: Experience Formation
categories.description: Selecting or deriving candidate experience from task-execution trajectories and their feedback. The survey distinguishes three forms by how the experience guides behaviour.

categories.title: Trajectory-Level Experience
categories.description: Trajectories kept as precedents, selected, annotated, compressed, or reconstructed for reuse.

categories.title: Semantic-Level Experience
categories.description: Lessons, insights, rules, and guidelines abstracted through reflection, trajectory comparison, and cross-trajectory generalization.

categories.title: Procedural-Level Experience
categories.description: Reusable workflows, skills, and programs extracted, synthesized, and verified from execution.

categories.title: Experience Organization
categories.description: Making retained experience accessible, from flat stores to trees, graphs, and hierarchical graphs.

categories.title: Flat Organization
categories.description: Independent entries keyed for direct lookup, ranking, or utility weighting.

categories.title: Tree-Structured Organization
categories.description: Index trees that organize access to records, and content trees that organize relations within guidance.

categories.title: Graph-Structured Organization
categories.description: Record graphs, transition graphs, and skill graphs that connect precedents, operations, and capabilities.

categories.title: Hierarchical Graph Organization
categories.description: Layered graphs that link units across roles, and nested graphs that open up the inside of a reusable unit.

categories.title: Experience Utilization
categories.description: Applying experience to current decisions: when to seek it, which to use, how to adapt it, how it shapes behaviour, and when to internalize it into model parameters.

categories.title: Experience Triggering
categories.description: Schedules, uncertainty signals, and learned policies that decide when to consult experience.

categories.title: Experience Selection
categories.description: Retrieval, reranking and filtering, and allocation of experience across multiple agents.

categories.title: Experience Adaptation
categories.description: Contextual grounding, guidance specialization, procedural reconfiguration, and feedback-guided revision before reuse.

categories.title: Experience Application
categories.description: How guidance shapes interpretation, generation, procedure reuse, decision-making, and evaluation.

categories.title: Experience Internalization
categories.description: Moving explicit guidance into model parameters through training on experience-shaped trajectories.

categories.title: Experience Maintenance
categories.description: Admitting, consolidating, revising, and retiring experience as evidence accumulates, and keeping its evolution safe.

categories.title: Experience Admission
categories.description: Success gates, consistency checks, and replay-based validation before experience enters the repository.

categories.title: Experience Consolidation
categories.description: Integrating repeated and related experience through targeted or region-level merging.

categories.title: Experience Refinement
categories.description: Diagnosing defects in retained guidance, revising it, and validating the revision.

categories.title: Experience Retirement
categories.description: Reducing the availability of stale or low-utility experience by pruning, down-weighting, or archiving.

categories.title: Coordinating Maintenance
categories.description: Learned or joint policies that align memory operations with formation and retrieval.

categories.title: Safeguarding Experience Evolution
categories.description: Poisoning attacks, provenance, rollback, repair, and unlearning for evolving experience.

categories.title: Evaluation and Benchmarks
categories.description: Evaluating intrinsic experience quality, the utilization process, and downstream effects, separating fixed experience reuse from feedback-driven sustained improvement and improvement of the learning mechanism.

categories.title: Scoring Reliability and Feedback Access
categories.description: Whether the scores and feedback that experience is learned and judged from can be trusted.

categories.title: Intrinsic Experience Quality
categories.description: Correctness, evidential support, coherence, and actionability of experience units and repositories.

categories.title: Utilization Process
categories.description: Scoring triggering, selection, adaptation, and application, and attributing behaviour to supplied experience.

categories.title: Downstream Effects and Transfer
categories.description: Immediate effectiveness of reuse, amortized cost, transfer, and harmful reuse.

categories.title: Sustained Improvement and Continual Learning
categories.description: Benchmarks for updating experience over streams, regression and forgetting, and meta-level learning.

categories.title: Applications
categories.description: Experience-driven agents in seven application settings.

categories.title: Question Answering
categories.description: Solution templates, search lessons, and tool-use procedures for QA and reasoning.

categories.title: Software Engineering
categories.description: Issue resolution, environment setup, and repair with trajectory- or human-derived experience.

categories.title: Computer Use
categories.description: Web, desktop, and mobile agents that retain workflows, skills, and interface knowledge.

categories.title: Recommender Systems
categories.description: User-level and shared guidance revised from recommendation feedback.

categories.title: Embodied Control
categories.description: Plans, skills, and lessons reused by embodied and robotic agents.

categories.title: Scientific Research
categories.description: Data science, machine-learning engineering, and AI-scientist agents.

categories.title: Financial Trading and Forecasting
categories.description: Reflection-driven trading and event forecasting agents.
